title: Quotient map associated to an intersection-refining open covering
statement: Let $X$ be the underlying topological space of a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal C$ be a collection of open subsets with $X=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal C}U$ and $U\cap V=\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal C,\,W\subset U\cap V}W$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal C$. Then there are a topological space $Y$ and a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ such that each $f(U)$ is open, $f^{-1}(f(U))=U$ for every $U\in\mathcal C$, and the opens $f(U)$ form a basis for the topology on $Y$. Here continuity means that inverse images of open sets are open, and a basis means a family of opens such that every open of $Y$ is a union of members.

source.place: Tag 0D5Q (topology-lemma-create-map-from-subcollection); specialized to the underlying topological space of a scheme

proof.text: Use ULift at universe level zero as a copy of the underlying set of X. Let B consist of the inverse images under ULift.down of the members of the given collection. Give this copy the topology generateFrom B and call the resulting topological space Y. Let f be ULift.up from X to Y. It is continuous by Mathlib continuous_generateFrom_iff: the inverse image of each generator is the corresponding original open subset of X.

Verify the three fields of Mathlib IsTopologicalBasis for B on Y. For a copied point in the inverse images of U and V, rewrite membership of its underlying point using the intersection-refinement equality and Opens.mem_sSup to obtain a member W containing that point and contained in U intersect V. Its inverse image in the copy gives the required basis refinement. For every copied point, the cover equality and Opens.mem_sSup give a member containing its underlying point; hence the union of B is the whole copied space. The generated-topology field is reflexivity.

Since ULift.up and ULift.down are inverse bijections, the image f(U) is the inverse image of U under ULift.down, and its inverse image under f is U. Each such generator is open in Y by GenerateOpen.basic. The family of images is therefore B, which is a basis by the preceding step. The type copy has the same universe as X. No nonempty-space or nonempty-family hypothesis was used.
